summary: Today’s pulse tracks Death toll from Philippines ferry fire rises to 76, with more still missing, Burial of King Oyo takes place in Uganda as news anchor prepares for throne, and Christopher Harborne matches £36m Reform donation of Ben Delo. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are reform, harborne, and party. In the background, French officials investigate if malicious act caused train derailment and Teen boy rescued after days adrift in Alaskan waters keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Death toll from Philippines ferry fire rises to 76, with more still missing
headlines.description: Access to the burnt-out boat has been slowed by toxic fumes and lingering heat, the country's coast guard says.

headlines.title: Burial of King Oyo takes place in Uganda as news anchor prepares for throne
headlines.description: Royal guards carry casket through streets of Fort Portal amid row over appointment of Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma Uganda’s King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, long the world’s youngest monarch, has been buried among the tombs of his royal forebears as ⁠his Tooro kingdom looked to put ⁠ a bitter succession battle behind ​it. Oyo’s appointed successor, the news anchor Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, cast nine coffee berries into the grave at the Karambi Royal Tombs, marking the formal handover of power in the western Ugandan kingdom.

headlines.title: Christopher Harborne matches £36m Reform donation of Ben Delo
headlines.description: Party leader, Nigel Farage, ‘humbled’ by contributions from billionaires as Harborne addresses ‘media speculation’ Analysis: donations of £72m make Reform’s prospects both rosier and riskier The cryptocurrency tycoon Christopher Harborne has given £36m to Reform UK, matching a donation from fellow billionaire Ben Delo . The pledges mean Reform has received a cash injection of £72m in just 24 hours. They are jointly the largest donations made to a UK political party and have intensified calls for restrictions on money received from individual donors.

headlines.title: French officials investigate if malicious act caused train derailment
headlines.description: Officials say a rail fragment was found on the tracks after Friday's crash of a passenger train that left 44 people injured.

headlines.title: Teen boy rescued after days adrift in Alaskan waters
headlines.description: The 15-year-old boy was rescued while the other two passengers from the capsized fishing vessel, his brother and cousin, died.

headlines.title: Donations of £72m make Reform’s prospects both rosier and riskier
headlines.description: Party can boost its campaign power with funds from billionaire backers, but it can also lose support from ordinary Britons All things being equal, pretty much any political strategist would welcome a £72m war chest; a sum higher than the combined spending of every major party at the 2024 general election. But all things are not equal, and with such a huge amount comes risk. Reform UK has been vocal in its arguments that two sudden £36m windfalls from billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne merely “levels the playing field” with the bigger parties when it comes to funding.

Here is what the news agency has reported: On Iran: War will end very soon.

headlinePool.title: Taxes wouldn’t fund $5,000 Trump ‘dividend’ if Republicans win midterms, says commerce secretary
headlinePool.description: Lutnick said $500bn of estimated $1tn needed to fund checks to all US adults could come from new visa program Donald Trump ’s controversial proposal to give a $5,000 “dividend” to all US adults if Republicans maintain control of Congress in November’s elections would not be paid out from US tax revenues, according to the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick. “It’s not tax money,” Lutnick said in an interview with NBC News , adding that the administration could “earn the money that Donald Trump wants to pay out, not from the deficit and not from taxpayers”.

headlinePool.title: Six Nigerians extradited to US over $6M online romance scam
headlinePool.description: Alleged members of Black Axe criminal network that swindled US women out of $6m flown from South Africa Six Nigerian nationals linked to an organized criminal network that allegedly swindled American women out of more than $6m through online romance scams were extradited to the United States on Friday. South African police confirmed they were to be extradited earlier on Friday, while local news in Africa confirmed that the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, known as the Hawks, facilitated their handover to officials from the US Federal Bureau of Investigation and Secret Service at Cape Town international airport, in collaboration with Interpol South Africa.

headlinePool.title: Jeremy Thomas, British producer of The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, dies aged 77
headlinePool.description: An outstanding figure in the UK film industry, Thomas was noted for collaborations with directors including Bernardo Bertolucci and David Cronenberg Jeremy Thomas, the distinguished British producer of films including Sexy Beast, High-Rise and the multi-Oscar-winning The Last Emperor, has died aged 77. A representative for Thomas said he died on Friday “peacefully, at his country home in Oxfordshire, surrounded by his family and loved ones”.

headlinePool.title: Saudi Arabia shuts down key oil pipeline, blaming drones from Iraq
headlinePool.description: Riyadh has increased use of East-West pipeline since start of war on Iran to bypass closure of strait of Hormuz Saudi Arabia has shut down a critical oil pipeline, accusing militants in Iraq of launching drone attacks on the export route being used to bypass the lockdown of the strait of Hormuz . The world’s largest ⁠crude oil exporter has increased its use of the 745-mile (1,200km) pipeline running across the Arabian Peninsula, which links Abqaiq, near the Gulf, to the port of Yanbu, on the Red Sea, since the US-Israeli war against Iran began.

headlinePool.title: A united Ireland would be 'fantastic' says Trump during Irish visit
headlinePool.description: Trump made the comments during a meeting with Irish leader Micheál Martin, but Downing Street says it will "stick to the Good Friday Agreement".

headlinePool.title: IDF soldier filmed shooting Palestinian in leg amid West Bank settler standoff
headlinePool.description: Incident is latest to raise questions over Israel’s ability or willingness to stop violent settlers in occupied territory An Israeli soldier shot a Palestinian man, wounding him in the leg, as settlers confronted villagers by grazing livestock on Palestinian-owned land in the town of Faqqua in the occupied West Bank. Eyewitnesses said that a group of settlers had entered the area with their livestock, prompting residents to try to stop them. Israeli forces then intervened and, according to men at the scene, opened fire at residents. One of them shot Qassem Hussam, a Palestinian man in his mid-30s, wounding him in the leg.

headlinePool.title: Nashville airport board unanimously approves name change to honor Dolly Parton
headlinePool.description: The city’s mayor and Tennessee’s governor threw their support behind the name change last month The Nashville airport is to be renamed after Dolly Parton , a board of commissioners voted on Friday, in tribute to the Smoky Mountain singer who is estimated to bring $1.8bn each year to Tennessee through her Dollywood theme park. The decision ensures that Parton, who died last month at 80 years old, will be memorialized with her name on an airport, although the renaming process will take time to complete.

headlinePool.title: Donald Trump says he would ‘love’ to see united Ireland
headlinePool.description: US president say on visit to republic that unification will happen eventually so ‘may as well happen now’ Donald Trump has said he would “love” to see a united Ireland and that it “may as well happen now”. The US president appeared to endorse the push for constitutional change on the island at the start of a two-day visit to Ireland on Saturday. The unexpected intervention prompted a swift rebuttal from the UK government and Northern Ireland’s unionist leaders.
